recentItems.title: Iraq restores ancient Assyrian artefacts damaged by ISIL in Mosul
recentItems.description:
Some of Iraq’s most significant archaeological treasures damaged by ISIL during its occupation have now been restored. 
ISIL’s propaganda videos, which circulated worldwide, showed its fighters destroying ancient Assyrian artefacts and blowing up historic sites. 
Since then, experts have painstakingly pieced together thousands of fragments to restore the damaged artefacts. 

Al Jazeera's Peter Smith has been given exclusive first access to view the completed restoration work.

recentItems.title: How Netanyahu reshaped Israel after 18 years in power
recentItems.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is known as the man with nine political lives.
He's held a vice grip on power for more than 18 years. 
That's made him Israel's longest-serving prime minister and its most polarising leader.
As people head to the polls next week for a general election, the vote is seen partly as a referendum on Netanyahu's leadership. 

Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh takes a look at the Netanyahu effect on the state of Israel.

Just a note that Al Jazeera is reporting on the Israeli elections from the occupied West Bank because it has been banned from reporting inside Israel.

recentItems.title: Russian strikes kill four in Kyiv as Zelenskyy seeks US air defence
recentItems.description:
Ukraine's ⁠President ⁠Volodymyr Zelenskyy says he's held constructive talks with ⁠US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. 
The talks reportedly focused on air defence and satellite communications after another night of Russian air strikes. 
Tensions between Zelenskyy and President Donald Trump have been simmering after accusations the US has restricted intelligence-sharing with Kyiv.
In the post, Zelenskyy mentioned the need for more defensive weapons and early warning systems to counter Russian attacks. 
He also mentioned that access to Starlink's network of satellites needs to be restored after Ukrainian officials said restrictions were disrupting military operations.  
Zelenskyy called for continued diplomatic efforts to end the war. 

Ukraine's emergency services say four people have been killed and others injured in Kyiv. 
Russian strikes sparked fires at a factory and warehouse in the Abukhivsky area south of the capital. 
Moscow's defence ministry says it also targeted critical facilities in other parts of Ukraine. 
The attacks struck vessels at the Reni Port on the Danube River and a cargo ship heading towards the city of Odesa on the Black Sea. 

And fires were burning on the Kyiv-Odesa highway, following a Russian drone attack. 
Several people have reportedly been killed. 
And early reports indicate a strike in Dnipro in the southeast has also caused casualties. 

Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine is in Kyiv for more on this and Yulia Shapovalova is monitoring developments from the Russian capital Moscow.

recentItems.title: US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is 'tending, not controlling' the Middle East
recentItems.description:
US special envoy Tom Barrack tells Al Jazeera that Washington will remain engaged in the Middle East but will no longer try to control it, insisting there are "no blanket guarantees" for allies. 

He says regional states must take greater responsibility for their own security, praises Qatar's role as a key intermediary with Iran, and calls for a ceasefire, mutual respect and calmer tensions. 

He's been speaking to Al Jazeera's Osama Bin Javaid at the Global Security Forum in Doha.
